newsitem.title: USA: Best Products to close stores, centers.
newsitem.headline: Best Products to close stores, centers.

text.p: Best Products Co. Inc., which filed for bankruptcy protection two weeks ago, said Monday it will close nearly half of its stores and lay off 4,500 workers in an effort to reposition its struggling retailing business.
The Richmond, Va.-based chain said it will close 81 of its 169 jewelry and home furnishings stores and three of its four distribution centres by the end of the year.
It plans to lay off 2,000 full-time employees and 2,500 part-time workers. Each store employs about 25 full-time and 30 part-time workers.

"We have carefully studied our business and we do not believe these locations will contribute significantly to the company's future profitability," said Daniel H. Levy, Best's chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

Levy said the company, suffering from declining sales and earnings and deteriorating supplier support, decided to make the announcement about the store closures now rather than dragging out the process.
"We believe it's in the best interests of the company and its associates to finalise closing plans now and remove questions about which locations will continue to operate," said Levy.
Most of the affected stores are in the western states of California, Oregon, Washington, Colorado and Texas.
When the closings are completed, Best will operate 88 stores in 17 states, compared with 169 in 23 states. The distribution centres being closed are in Seattle, Las Vegas, and Denver.

Best filed for Chapter 11 protection -- its second trip through bankruptcy court -- on Sept. 24 after Ocean Reef Management Inc., a merchant and investment banking firm, withdrew its $63.2 million takeover offer. It first filed in January 1991 and emerged in June 1994.
Best Products' stock edged up 7.8 cents to 37.5 cents early on Nasdaq.
